content.text: I want to assess how much space is consumed by the hermes profiles real quick. I saw we have got 40 some profiles on this bad boy

The [Clanker Hermes profiles](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/.local/hermes-lab/home/profiles) currently consume **795 MiB**, about **0.83 GB**.

| What’s taking space | Usage |
|---|---:|
| Browser data | 521 MiB |
| Workspace tools, mostly a Node installation | 234 MiB |
| Databases, logs, caches, everything else | 39 MiB |

**Current count:** 11 named profiles plus the default. There are also **34 deleted-profile markers**, occupying just **136 KiB**.

The two largest profiles account for **80%** of profile storage. The entire Hermes home, including default/shared data, uses **925 MiB**.

Verified without following symlinks. Nothing deleted.

alright why we are using hermes profiles in clanker? for acc isolation right? so that when one user tasks clanker to do some browser thing, it doesn't pulls the context from the other user's profile. right?

Yes: Hermes profiles separate **agent context**: histories/state DB, memories, workspace and related files. Fresh profile provisioning deliberately avoids copying other users’ memories, credentials or cookies ([runtime/slack_workspace.py:165](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/slack_workspace.py:165)).

**Browser/account isolation also has its own enforcement**:

- Browser context is bound to verified Slack workspace + requester + resolved Hermes home; conflicting session ownership is rejected ([service.py:33](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/service.py:33)).
- Kernel checks ownership of the underlying browser endpoint, rejects persistent/shared provider profiles, and verifies the remote browser identity ([kernel.py:68](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/kernel.py:68)).
- Native browser tools require the authenticated task and profile home to match ([native_browser.py:48](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/seatbelt/native_browser.py:48)).
- Current configuration disables local browser fallback and real browser profile reuse ([install.py:68](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/seatbelt/install.py:68)).

So: **profiles keep private agent context separate; the browser/vault ownership checks keep accounts separate. Profiles alone are insufficient.** This is verified from current source, without checking deployment activation or running a live cross-user test.
